verdict.rationale: pnpm's own docs call it a "drop-in replacement for npm" that works on any existing project with no migration. It also offers a `hoisted` nodeLinker that builds an npm/Yarn Classic-style node_modules, and the feature-comparison page shows npm-parallel commands such as `pnpm sbom` alongside `npm sbom`. However, the evidence never documents command-by-command parity, and one hands-on user found pnpm's commands "a little fussier to use" than Yarn 1, a mild caveat rather than a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: documented mapping of npm/yarn commands and flags to pnpm equivalents, explicit statement of CLI/interface compatibility beyond the marketing claim, independent corroboration that familiar commands work unchanged.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can keep using familiar commands and interface conventions from the incumbent tool while adopting this manager

citations.quote: pnpm is a drop-in replacement for npm. Point it at any existing project — no migration, no rewrites, no lockfile gymnastics.
set the nodeLinker setting to `hoisted`. This will instruct pnpm to create a node_modules directory that is similar to those created by npm and Yarn Classic.
